title: Floor calendar and GI Bill story
materials: Painter’s tape for a 12-month floor grid
Holiday cards and origin cards, one set per patrol

displayContent.headline: Build the calendar
displayContent.body: Put each holiday card on the right month. Then match each holiday to its origin card.

prompts.text: What’s the difference between Memorial Day and Veterans Day?
prompts.answer: Memorial Day honors those who died in service. Veterans Day thanks everyone who served, living or dead. (Armed Forces Day honors those serving now.)

prompts.text: Which of these days are federal holidays?
prompts.answer: Only two: Memorial Day and Veterans Day. The rest are observances, not days off.

prompts.text: The GI Bill, 1944: how might your grandparents’ or great-grandparents’ lives have been different without it?
prompts.answer: It paid for about 2.3 million veterans to go to college and backed 4.3 million home loans by 1955.

leaderScript: Tape a 12-month grid on the floor before the meeting.
Patrols place the holiday cards on the right months, then match each to an origin card.
Press → for the answer key and R to show it while you score.
Press → for the key question: Memorial Day versus Veterans Day. Drill the answer until they can say it back.

Close the station with a two-minute GI Bill story: President Roosevelt signed it on June 22, 1944. It paid for college or job training, helped veterans buy homes, and gave unemployment pay. Then ask the question on screen.
Trivia if there’s time: Veterans Day moved to the fourth Monday in October in 1971. People didn’t like it, and it went back to November 11 in 1978.

discussionQuestions.question: Why is Veterans Day on November 11?
discussionQuestions.answer: It began as Armistice Day: World War I’s fighting stopped at the eleventh hour of the eleventh day of the eleventh month of 1918. Congress made it a legal holiday in 1938 and renamed it Veterans Day in 1954.

discussionQuestions.question: What’s today’s version of the GI Bill?
discussionQuestions.answer: The Post-9/11 GI Bill, which helps veterans pay for school or job training.

reveal.title: Answer key: military holidays and observances

cells: Decoration Day: Gen. John A. Logan’s order set May 30, 1868; moved to a Monday in 1971
All who served, living or dead
Armistice Day, for the end of World War I’s fighting in 1918; legal holiday 1938; renamed 1954
First held in 1950 to replace each branch’s separate day; not a day off
Prisoners of war and the missing
Gold Star Mother’s and Family’s Day
Families who lost a service member
Created by Congress in 1994; observance, not a holiday

ifShortOnTime: Skip the origin cards: place holidays on months only, then go straight to the Memorial Day versus Veterans Day question. Keep the GI Bill story to one minute.
lowVolunteerNote: With two leaders, run this and the academy sort as side-by-side stations and swap patrols at 0:40.
